title: Exercise 7A · Q10(b)
summary: Form an equation in c from ΔMPQ, solve for c, then find NQ in ΔNPQ.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q10(b): In the figure, ∠MPQ = 90°, MN = 3c, NP = 4c, PQ = 25 cm and MQ = 39 cm. Find the values of c and d, where d = NQ.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In the figure, **∠MPQ = 90°**. **MN = 3c** and **NP = 4c**. **PQ = 25 cm** and **MQ = 39 cm**. We have to find **c** and **d**, where **d = NQ**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In **ΔMPQ**, **∠P = 90°**, so the hypotenuse is **MQ**. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{MQ^2} &= \role{legA}{MP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length (MP = 7c).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{MQ^2} &= \role{legA}{MP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2} \\ \role{hyp}{39^2} &= \role{legA}{(7c)^2} + \role{legB}{25^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Solve for c²
steps.narration: Move the number to the left side, then divide by 49.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{MQ^2} &= \role{legA}{MP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2} \\ \role{hyp}{39^2} &= \role{legA}{(7c)^2} + \role{legB}{25^2} \\ \role{hyp}{1521} &= \role{legA}{49c^2} + \role{legB}{625} \\ 49c^2 &= 1521 - 625 = 896 \\ c^2 &= \frac{896}{49}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Take the square root
steps.narration: A length is positive, so take the positive root. We keep extra digits for the next step.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{MQ^2} &= \role{legA}{MP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2} \\ \role{hyp}{39^2} &= \role{legA}{(7c)^2} + \role{legB}{25^2} \\ \role{hyp}{1521} &= \role{legA}{49c^2} + \role{legB}{625} \\ 49c^2 &= 1521 - 625 = 896 \\ c^2 &= \frac{896}{49} \\ c &= \frac{\sqrt{896}}{7} = \role{ans}{4.28\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square of NP
steps.narration: In ΔNPQ we need **NP²**. Use **c² = 896/49** from before.\[\begin{aligned}NP^2 &= (4c)^2 = 16c^2 \\ &= 16 \times \frac{896}{49} = 292.6\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔNPQ, **∠P = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **NQ**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{NQ^2} &= \role{legA}{NP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{NQ^2} &= \role{legA}{NP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{292.6} + \role{legB}{25^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{292.6} + \role{legB}{625} \\ &= \role{hyp}{917.6}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 917.6 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{NQ^2} &= \role{legA}{NP^2} + \role{legB}{PQ^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{292.6} + \role{legB}{25^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{292.6} + \role{legB}{625} \\ &= \role{hyp}{917.6} \\ \role{hyp}{NQ} &= \sqrt{917.6} = \role{ans}{30.3\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: MP in terms of c
challenges.prompt: MN = 3c and NP = 4c. What is the length of **MP**?
challenges.hint: MP is the whole segment from M to P.

takeaways: When lengths are given in terms of **c**, write Pythagoras' theorem with c in it and **solve the equation** for c.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
